segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: As he was going out of the temple, one of his disciples said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Teacher, look! What stones, and what buildings!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And Jesus said to him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Do you see these great buildings? Not one stone will be left here on another that will not be thrown down.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: As he was sitting on the Mount of Olives opposite the temple, Peter, James, John and Andrew asked him privately,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Tell us, when will these things be, and what will be the sign when all these things are about to be accomplished?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus began to say to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Watch out that no one leads you astray.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am he,’ and they will lead many astray.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: When you hear of wars and rumors of wars, do not be alarmed. It must happen, but the end is not yet.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For nation will rise against nation and kingdom against kingdom; there will be earthquakes in place after place; there will be famines. These things are the beginning of the birth pains.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But you, watch out for yourselves. They will hand you over to councils, and you will be beaten in synagogues, and you will stand before governors and kings because of me, as a testimony to them.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And the good news must first be proclaimed to all the nations.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And when they lead you away to hand you over, do not worry beforehand about what you will say, but say whatever is given to you in that hour, for it is not you who are speaking but the Holy Spirit.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Brother will hand brother over to death, and a father his child, and children will rise up against parents and have them put to death.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And you will be hated by everyone because of my name. But the one who endures to the end will be saved.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But when you see the abomination of desolation standing where he must not be”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: (let the reader understand)

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “then those in Judea must flee to the mountains;

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: the one on the housetop must not come down or go in to take anything out of his house,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: and the one in the field must not turn back to get his cloak.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Woe to those who are pregnant and to those who are nursing in those days!

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Pray that it may not happen in winter.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For those days will be a distress such as has never been, from the beginning of the creation that God created until now, and never will be.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And if the Lord had not cut short the days, no flesh would have been saved. But for the sake of the chosen, whom he chose, he has cut short the days.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And then if anyone says to you, ‘Look, here is the Messiah!’ or ‘Look, there he is!’ do not believe it.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For false messiahs and false prophets will arise and will give signs and wonders, to lead astray, if possible, the chosen.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But you, watch out. I have told you everything beforehand.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But in those days, after that distress, the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: and the stars will be falling from the sky, and the powers in the heavens will be shaken.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And then they will see the Son of Man coming in clouds with great power and glory.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And then he will send out the angels and gather the chosen from the four winds, from the end of the earth to the end of the sky.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Learn the parable from the fig tree: when its branch has already become tender and puts out its leaves, you know that summer is near.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: So also you, when you see these things happening, know that he is near, at the doors.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Truly I tell you, this generation will certainly not pass away until all these things have taken place.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will never pass away.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But about that day or hour no one knows, not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but only the Father.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Watch out, stay alert, for you do not know when the time is.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: It is like a man away on a journey: he left his house and gave authority to his slaves, to each his work, and he commanded the doorkeeper to stay awake.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: So stay awake, for you do not know when the master of the house is coming, whether in the evening or at midnight or at cockcrow or at dawn,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: so that he does not come suddenly and find you sleeping.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And what I say to you I say to everyone: stay awake.”

notes.note: The Greek is simply “I am.” Most take it as a claim to be the Messiah, which is how Matthew's parallel spells it out. Some hear an echo of the divine self-designation of the Greek Old Testament, so that the impostors claim more than a title.

The same Greek word lies behind “nation” here, “nations” in verse 10, and “Gentiles” elsewhere in this translation. In verse 10 “all the nations” could also be heard as “all the Gentiles”; the wider sense is chosen because the scope is the whole world.

notes.traditional: for a testimony against them / as a witness to them
notes.note: The Greek dative can mean testimony given to the rulers or testimony that will count against them. Translations divide. The link with verse 10, where the good news is proclaimed to all nations, favours “to them,” but the hostile sense is possible.

The phrase comes from Daniel (9:27; 11:31; 12:11), where it refers to a sacrilege that defiles the temple and leaves it desolate. Jewish readers connected it with the pagan altar that Antiochus IV set up in the Jerusalem temple in 167 BC. Jesus uses it for a comparable outrage still to come; what event is meant is debated.

notes.phrase: standing where he must not be
notes.note: The Greek noun for “abomination” is neuter, but the participle “standing” is masculine, which suggests that Mark has a person in view. Many translations nevertheless use “it.” The grammatical mismatch is deliberate enough that “he” is kept here.

Most scholars take this as Mark's own aside to whoever reads his book aloud, signalling that the cryptic phrase needs decoding. It is treated here as the narrator's words. The alternative is that Jesus himself is speaking, referring to the reader of Daniel.

The Greek word is an ordinary term for severe pressure, hardship or suffering. “Tribulation” has become a technical term in some end-times schemes, which it was not for the first readers. The wording echoes Daniel 12:1.

The traditional “the elect” hides the fact that the noun and the verb are the same word in Greek and now sounds like a doctrinal term. In the Septuagint the word describes Israel as the people God chose. “The chosen” is used again in verses 22 and 27.

The Greek word is traditionally rendered “Christ.” Here it is a title, the anointed king Israel expected, rather than a name for Jesus, so “Messiah” is used; “false messiahs” in verse 22 follows suit. Several modern translations make the same distinction in the Gospels.

notes.phrase: the Son of Man coming in clouds
notes.note: The language is drawn from Daniel 7:13, where “one like a son of man” comes with the clouds of heaven and is given everlasting dominion. The darkened sun and moon and the falling stars in verses 24–25 likewise echo the prophets (Isaiah 13:10; 34:4), who used such imagery for God's judgment on nations.

notes.traditional: it is near / he is near
notes.note: The Greek verb has no expressed subject, so “it is near” (the end, or the event just described) is equally possible. “He” is chosen because the Son of Man has just been mentioned and because the image of someone at the doors is picked up in the returning master of verses 34–36.

The most natural sense is Jesus's own contemporaries, and that is how the phrase is used elsewhere in Mark. Because this is hard to reconcile with the coming of the Son of Man, others have proposed the Jewish people, humanity, or the generation that sees the signs. It is also disputed whether “all these things” covers the whole discourse or only the events leading to the temple's destruction in AD 70.
Most manuscripts add “and pray” after “stay alert.” A few early witnesses lack the words, and the Greek text followed here omits them as a probable addition influenced by 14:38.

The Greek word means a slave, someone owned by a master, not a hired servant. Many English versions soften it to “servants.” The household Jesus describes is one in which the owner's slaves run his affairs in his absence.

notes.phrase: whether in the evening or at midnight or at cockcrow or at dawn
notes.note: These are the popular names of the four watches into which the Roman system divided the night, each about three hours long. The master may return during any of them.

candidates.reason: Recurs across the Gospels, Paul and Revelation, where translators vary between tribulation, affliction, suffering, trouble and distress, and “tribulation” carries end-times baggage.
“Elect” versus “chosen” affects many passages in the Gospels and letters, and the link with the verb ἐκλέγομαι should be visible consistently.
Very frequent across the New Testament and translations split between “servant”, “slave” and “bondservant”; readers would be misled by variation.
“Gospel” versus “good news” needs one decision for the whole New Testament, including the related verb εὐαγγελίζομαι.
The word is rendered “betray”, “deliver up”, “hand over” or “arrest” in different versions, and the Passion narratives and Paul depend on the reader seeing that it is one verb.
